fatal_errors: Laser cladding does not reconstruct the target intervention or temperature-controlled nanoindentation/friction protocol.
The proposed mechanism is generic and omits the target transition from stacking-fault/dislocation-mediated deformation to lattice disorder above approximately 900 K.
No actual operating limits, temperature threshold, velocity range, or wear-depth range are defined.
The falsification experiment is only a placeholder and specifies no microscopic deformation measurements.
The cited study concerns Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi on an AZ91D matrix and compares the coating with the substrate, not laser-cladded versus unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu under identical conditions.
explanation: The response identifies the broad material and wear-resistance problem and names an unchanged coating as a comparator, but it neither reconstructs the target simulation nor supplies a testable alternative. It misses the specified atomic geometry, indentation protocol, temperatures, boundary conditions, and the predicted stability through 600 K followed by sharp softening and increased friction at 900–1200 K. Its claimed microstructural mechanism, limits, and falsification experiment are unspecified. The citation offers only indirect evidence that a different laser-cladded HEA coating can outperform a magnesium substrate; it does not establish that laser cladding improves an existing FeNiCrCoCu/Cu coating relative to the unchanged coating.
